items.title: The flat model spacetime: the Minkowski metric on R^4 and its inertial chart
items.statement:
Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ carry its standard smooth structure
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and let
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ be the **identity chart**, $x(p)=p$;
it is a global chart of the maximal smooth atlas, and the coordinate
derivations $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ form a basis of
$T_pM$ at every $p\in M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). Write

$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$$

for the standard Lorentz form of inertia $(3,1,0)$ in this basis
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

**(a) The metric.** Define the covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$ by the
requirement that its components in the identity chart are the constants

$$g_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}\qquad(a,b=0,1,2,3),$$

that is, $g_p(\partial_a|_p,\partial_b|_p)=\eta_{ab}$ for every $p\in M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] clause (a)). The component
functions are constant, hence $C^\infty$, so $g$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field; at every $p$ the form $g_p$ is nondegenerate with
inertia $(3,1,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a) the
pair $(M,g)$ is therefore a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$.

**(b) The inertial chart and frame.** The chart $x$ is called the **inertial
chart** of the flat model. In this chart the coordinate frame
$(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is a $g$-orthonormal frame at
every point, $g(\partial_a,\partial_b)=\eta_{ab}$; it is simultaneously a
coordinate frame and a **tetrad field** in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], defined on all of $M$.

**(c) Time orientation and causal classification.** Define the smooth vector
field $N:=\partial_0$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)=\eta_{00}=-1<0$ for every $p$, the field $N$ is everywhere
timelike, so $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). For a nonzero tangent
vector $v=v^a\partial_a|_p$ the definitions of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c) and
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] give

$$g_p(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2,\qquad g_p(v,N_p)=-v^0 .$$

so $v$ is **future-directed** exactly when $v^0>0$, and

- $v$ is future timelike $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2>\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is future null $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2=\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is spacelike $\iff$ $(v^0)^2<\sum_i(v^i)^2$;

consequently the future causal cone at every point is
$\{v\neq0: v^0\ge\sqrt{\sum_i(v^i)^2}\}$. These are the standard readings of
the Minkowski form in the inertial chart; the chain of equivalences is the
specialization of the causal classification to this pair $(g_p,N_p)$ and is
recorded here for later use.

**(d) Scope.** This item defines geometric data only: a manifold, a metric
field, a time orientation and a distinguished chart and frame. It makes no
claim about curvature, about any field equation, about which geometry a
physical model uses, or about nature; the physical reading of the data, the
dimensions of the coordinates and the numerical values or signs of physical
constants belong to the framework's unit conventions and postulates, which
are separate items. In particular no relation between the coordinate
functions $x^a$ and physical time or length measurements is asserted here.

items.title: The flat model: vanishing connection and curvature, translation Killing fields and straight geodesics
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with its inertial chart $x$,
and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Vanishing connection.** In the inertial chart all Christoffel symbols
of $\nabla$ vanish identically:

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\equiv0\qquad(a,b,c=0,1,2,3).$$

**(b) Vanishing curvature.** The curvature operator of $\nabla$ vanishes
identically, $R\equiv0$; consequently the curvature components, the Ricci
tensor, the scalar curvature and the Einstein tensor vanish identically,

$$R^a{}_{bcd}\equiv0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\equiv0,\qquad S\equiv0,\qquad G_{ab}\equiv0 .$$

**(c) Translation Killing fields.** Each coordinate field $\partial_a$ is a
Killing field of $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]]); in particular the time
orientation field $N=\partial_0$ is a unit timelike Killing field.

**(d) Straight geodesics.** A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ on an interval
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) is a geodesic of $\nabla$ if and
only if there are $x_0,v\in\mathbb R^4$ such that

$$x\bigl(\gamma(s)\bigr)=x_0+s\,v\qquad(s\in I).$$

For such a geodesic the speed is constant,
$g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2$; the maximal
geodesic with $x(\gamma(0))=x_0$ and $x(\gamma)'(0)=v$ has domain
$\mathbb R$. If $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $v^0>0$, the geodesic is a future timelike
worldline
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) and, for any $s_0\in I$,
the parameter
$\tau(s):=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}\,(s-s_0)/c$ is proper time up to an additive
constant, with $d\gamma/d\tau$ the physical four-velocity
$U$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$
([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]] clause 3).

**(e) Inertial-chart velocity reading.** Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic as in
(d) with $x(\gamma(s))=x_0+sv$, $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $v^0>0$. Define
$t(s):=x^0(\gamma(s))/c=(x_0^0+sv^0)/c$; this is strictly increasing, and
on $t(I)$ define
$\gamma_t(t):=\gamma((ct-x_0^0)/v^0)$. Then
$x(\gamma_t(t))=(ct,\mathbf q(t))$ for its spatial component $\mathbf q$,
and the coordinate velocity is the constant vector
$\mathbf w:=d\mathbf q/dt=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$. With
$|\mathbf w|:=\|\mathbf w\|_2$ from the Euclidean inner product
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), timelikeness gives $|\mathbf w|<c$.

items.title: Flat linearized perturbations: families, trace reversal, gauge transformation and harmonic gauge
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant metric components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set, identified with its image under
$x$; all components below are taken in the inertial chart. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Flat linearized family.** A **flat linearized family over $\Omega$**
consists of a number $\varepsilon_1>0$, a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $h$ on $\Omega$ with components $h_{ab}$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) — the **first-order
perturbation** — and a smooth family $q$ of symmetric component fields
$q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$, defined for $\lambda\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
and $p\in\Omega$, such that for every $\lambda$ with
$0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\lambda,p):=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}(p)+\lambda^2\,q_{ab}(\lambda,p)$$

is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\lambda)$ on
$\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$; $q$ is the **normalized remainder**. The
family is thus normalized so that $g(0)=\eta$ is its value at
$\lambda=0$ and $h=\partial_\lambda g(\lambda)|_{\lambda=0}$. No assumption
is made that $g(\lambda)$ solves any field equation; the metrics $g(\lambda)$
are the mathematical input of the linearization.

**(b) First-order coefficients.** Let $A(\lambda)$ stand for any of the
component families $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))$,
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))$, $S(g(\lambda))$,
$G_{ab}(g(\lambda))$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\lambda)$; these
are smooth in $(\lambda,p)$ because the Christoffel symbols, the curvature
components and the inverse metric are smooth functions of the metric
components and their derivatives
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Define the **first-order
coefficients**

$$\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}:=\partial_\lambda\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\quad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},$$
$$S^{(1)}:=\partial_\lambda S(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0},\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}:=\partial_\lambda G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\big|_{\lambda=0}.$$

**(c) Index conventions.** Indices on first-order quantities are raised and
lowered with the flat metric $\eta$ and its inverse $\eta^{ab}$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]): $\partial^a:=\eta^{ab}\partial_b$,
$h^{ab}:=\eta^{ac}\eta^{bd}h_{cd}$, and

$$\Box:=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b=-\partial_0^2+\partial_1^2+\partial_2^2+\partial_3^2$$

is the **d'Alembertian** of the flat metric, applied componentwise to
component families. The **trace** of $h$ and the **trace-reversed
perturbation** are

$$h:=\eta^{ab}h_{ab},\qquad \bar h_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,h\,\eta_{ab} .$$

The inverse passage is the same formula, $\bar h_{ab}$'s trace being
$\eta^{ab}\bar h_{ab}=h-2h=-h$: explicitly

$$h_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\eta^{cd}\bar h_{cd} .$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For a smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on
$\Omega$ define the **gauge-transformed first-order perturbation**

$$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a .$$

This is the first-order perturbation of the pullback family
$\Phi_{-\lambda}^*g(\lambda)$ along the local flows $\Phi_s$ of the vector
field $\xi^a=\eta^{ab}\xi_b$, that is, the perturbation produced by the
infinitesimal chart change $x'^a=x^a+\lambda\xi^a$ and re-read on the fixed
inertial chart; the transformation of the metric components displayed here
is the linearization of the Jacobian transformation law, and
its consequences for $\bar h$ and for $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}$, $S^{(1)}$
and $G^{(1)}$ are proved separately on this page (the first-order curvature
and gauge theorem that follows this definition).
The perturbation $h$ is **in harmonic gauge** (also called de Donder gauge)
when

$$\partial^a\bar h_{ab}=0 .$$

**(e) Scope.** This item fixes the objects of the flat linearization: the
normalized family, the first-order coefficients defined as exact
$\lambda$-derivatives, the trace reversal, the d'Alembertian and the gauge
transformation. It asserts no explicit formula for the first-order
coefficients, no existence of a gauge representative satisfying (d), no
solution of any linearized field equation and no physical interpretation;
those are separate results. The notation is tied to the inertial chart: a
change of chart is a different operation from the gauge transformation (d),
which changes the metric family inside the fixed chart.

items.title: First-order curvature of a flat linearized family, gauge transformations and the quadratic remainder
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be an open set of the flat model
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]], let
$(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over $\Omega$ with
first-order coefficients $\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}$,
$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}$, $S^{(1)}$, $G^{(1)}_{ab}$ and with trace
reversal $\bar h$, d'Alembertian $\Box$ and gauge transformation
$h'_{ab}=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$ as in
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]], and let $L>0$ be a length scale.
All components are taken in the inertial chart and all contractions are
with $\eta$ and $\eta^{-1}$.

**(a) Christoffel symbols.** For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there is a
constant $C_K<\infty$ such that for all $p\in K$ and
$0<|\lambda|\le\varepsilon_1/2$,

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \Gamma^{(1)a}{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,\eta^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bh_{cd}+\partial_ch_{bd}-\partial_dh_{bc}\bigr).$$

**(b) Ricci tensor.** With the same constants (enlarged if necessary),

$$\Bigl|\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}=\tfrac12\bigl(\partial_c\partial_a h^{c}{}_{b}+\partial_c\partial_b h^{c}{}_{a}-\Box h_{ab}-\partial_a\partial_b h\bigr).$$

**(c) Scalar curvature and Einstein tensor.** With the same constants,

$$\Bigl|S(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,S^{(1)}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad S^{(1)}=\partial_a\partial_bh^{ab}-\Box h,$$

and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\lambda,p)-\lambda\,G^{(1)}_{ab}(p)\Bigr|\le C_K\,\lambda^2,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h_{ab}+\partial^c\partial_{(a}\bar h_{b)c}-\tfrac12\,\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\partial^d\bar h_{cd}.$$

**(d) Gauge transformation.** For every smooth covector field $\xi$ on
$\Omega$,

$$\bar h'{}_{ab}=\bar h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a+\eta_{ab}\,\partial^c\xi_c,\qquad \partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}-\Box\xi_b .$$

Consequently $h'$ is in harmonic gauge exactly when
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and in that case

$$G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab}.$$

**(e) Gauge invariance of the first-order curvature.** For every smooth
covector field $\xi$ on $\Omega$,

$$\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}(h),\qquad S^{(1)}(h')=S^{(1)}(h),\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=G^{(1)}_{ab}(h).$$

That is, subtracting the pure-gauge perturbation
$\partial_a\xi_b+\partial_b\xi_a$ from the first-order perturbation leaves
the first-order Ricci, scalar and Einstein tensors unchanged; their
first-order coefficients depend on $h$ only through its gauge-equivalence
class.

**(f) Quadratic remainder.** In this clause, suprema of the nonnegative
component magnitudes over an empty set are defined to be $0$. For every compact $K\subseteq\Omega$ there are
$\delta_0>0$ and $C_K<\infty$ such that for every smooth symmetric component
field $A=(A_{ab})$ on a neighborhood of $K$ with

$$B_K(A):=\sup_K\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|+L\sup_K\max_{a,b,c}|\partial_cA_{ab}|+L^2\sup_K\max_{a,b,c,d}|\partial_c\partial_dA_{ab}|\le\delta_0,$$

the metric $\eta+A$ is Lorentzian of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $K$ and

$$\Bigl|G_{ab}(\eta+A)(p)-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)(p)\Bigr|\le \frac{C_K\,B_K(A)^2}{L^2}\qquad(p\in K),$$

where $G^{(1)}_{ab}(A)$ is the right-hand side of the displayed formula of
(c) with $h$ replaced by $A$, and $G_{ab}(\eta+A)$ is the Einstein tensor of
the metric with components $\eta_{ab}+A_{ab}$.

items.title: All-space smooth wave equation with zero data, and harmonic gauge on flat space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, as carried by
the cited polar-surface and divergence suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]],
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]). Let
$\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq
\mathbb R^3$, with $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ as established in [F1]
([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]],
[[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]],
[[thm-volume-recursion-for-closed-euclidean-balls]],
[[thm-jordan-measurable-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable-with-equal-content]],
[[cor-volume-of-a-closed-three-ball]]), let $c>0$ be a real parameter, and
let $\Delta$ be the Laplacian of $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

**(a) Spherical means.** For $f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, signed
$r\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$ define

$$M_rf(x):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{S^2}f(x+r\omega)\,d\sigma(\omega),\qquad H_f(x,s):=s\,M_{cs}f(x).$$

Then $Mf:(x,r)\mapsto M_rf(x)$ and $H_f$ are $C^\infty$ on
$\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$,
$M_{-r}f=M_rf$, $M_0f=f$, $\partial_x^\alpha M_rf=M_r(\partial^\alpha f)$ for every multiindex
$\alpha$, and for every $r>0$

$$r^2\,\partial_rM_rf(x)=\frac1{4\pi}\int_{B_r(x)}\Delta f(y)\,dy\quad(r>0),\qquad \partial_r^2M_rf+\frac2r\,\partial_rM_rf=\Delta M_rf\quad(r\ne0).$$

Moreover $H_f(x,0)=0$, $\partial_sH_f(x,0)=f(x)$ and
$(c^{-2}\partial_s^2-\Delta_x)H_f=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$.

**(b) Duhamel solution with zero data.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an
open interval, $t_0\in I$ and $F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times I)$. Then

$$u(x,t):=c^2\int_{t_0}^tH_{F(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv\qquad((x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times I)$$

is $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times I$, satisfies
$u(\cdot,t_0)=0$, $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and

$$(c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta_x)u=F\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^3\times I,$$

and every partial derivative of $u$ is bounded on $K\times[a,b]$ for every
compact $K\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and every compact interval
$[a,b]\subseteq I$.

**(c) Harmonic gauge.** Let $h$ be a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor
field on $\mathbb R^4$ with components $h_{ab}$ in the identity chart, let
$\bar h$ be its trace reverse and set
$F_b:=-\partial^a\bar h_{ab}\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^4)$
([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clauses (b)-(c)). Then there is a
smooth covector field $\xi_b$ on $\mathbb R^4$ with
$\Box\xi_b=\partial^a\bar h_{ab}$, and for
$h'_{ab}:=h_{ab}-\partial_a\xi_b-\partial_b\xi_a$,

$$\partial^a\bar h'{}_{ab}=0,\qquad G^{(1)}_{ab}(h')=-\tfrac12\,\Box\bar h'{}_{ab},$$

where $G^{(1)}$ is the first-order Einstein coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] clause (b).

items.title: Stationary weak-field data: the diagonal ansatz, its bounds, stationarity and the Einstein-family condition
items.statement:
Let $(M,g_\eta,N_\eta)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ and constant components
$\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $\Omega\subseteq M$ be a
nonempty open spacetime region, identified with its image in $\mathbb R^4$,
and let $\pi:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be the spatial projection
$\pi(x^0,\mathbf x)=\mathbf x$. Its image $U:=\pi(\Omega)$ is open: a
coordinate ball in $\Omega$ about any point projects onto a ball about that
point's spatial coordinates. Let $K\subseteq U$ be compact. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N>0$ be the constants of the framework's conventions and put
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$. The coordinates have units of metres, $c$ has units
$\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, and $\varepsilon$ is dimensionless.

**(a) Structural data.** A tuple $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is
**stationary weak-field data** when

- $L>0$ is a length, $C>0$ is dimensionless, and $\varepsilon_0>0$ is
  dimensionless;
- $\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth dimensionless spatial function and
  $r=(r_{ab})$ is a family of smooth dimensionless spatial functions
  $r_{ab}:(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)\times U\to\mathbb R$ for some
  $\varepsilon_1>\varepsilon_0$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]);
- for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)=\begin{cases}-(1+2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))+r_{00}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=b=0,\\[2pt] r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&\{a,b\}=\{0,i\},\\[2pt] (1-2\varepsilon\varphi(\pi(p)))\,\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\pi(p)),&a=i,\ b=j,\end{cases}$$

  is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\varepsilon)$ on
  $\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
- **(spatial factorization and stationarity)** all metric components factor
  through $\pi$ by construction. Thus points of $\Omega$ with the same
  spatial coordinates have the same metric components, even when they lie in
  different connected components of that spatial fiber, and
  $\partial_0g_{ab}=0$ on $\Omega$;
- **(spatial bounds)** for every multiindex $\alpha\in\mathbb N^3$ with
  $|\alpha|\le2$ and every $\mathbf x\in K$,

$$|\partial^\alpha\varphi(\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{00}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|+|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{0i}(\varepsilon,\mathbf x)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^{|\alpha|}}.$$

  (Derivatives are with respect to $x^1,x^2,x^3$; here $|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}|$
  is the maximum over $i,j$ and $|\partial^\alpha r_{0i}|$ is the maximum
  over $i$.)

**(b) Derived data.** For stationary weak-field data define the
**spatial potential**

$$\Phi:=\varepsilon c^2\varphi\qquad\text{on }U,$$

a smooth spatial function of dimension $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ in the
framework's unit conventions; its pullback to $\Omega$ is stationary. The
symmetric component family $g(\varepsilon)-\eta$ is the **perturbation of the
family**.

**(c) Einstein families.** Stationary weak-field data form an **Einstein
family with coupling $\kappa$** when for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$
there is a smooth symmetric component field $T_{ab}(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ on
$\Omega$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) satisfying

$$G_{ab}\bigl(g(\varepsilon)\bigr)=\kappa\,T_{ab}(\varepsilon)\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection of
$g(\varepsilon)$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). In that case define the
**spatial density read from the time-time component**

$$\rho_\varepsilon(\mathbf x):=\frac{T_{00}(\varepsilon,x^0,\mathbf x)}{c^2}\qquad\text{on }U,$$

where any $x^0$ with $(x^0,\mathbf x)\in\Omega$ may be used. This is
well-defined: the metric is the pullback of spatial functions, so its
coordinate curvature components, and hence $T_{00}=\kappa^{-1}G_{00}$, are
constant on each fiber of $\pi$, including when that fiber is disconnected.
It has units $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; it is a coordinate-component
density and is not thereby the dust rest-mass density.

**(d) Scope.** This item fixes a class of metric families and the vocabulary
of the weak-field bridge: the spatial factorization, component form,
stationarity, spatial derivative bounds, potential, and the equation that
upgrades the data to an Einstein family. It asserts neither existence for prescribed data nor that $\partial_0$ is
timelike or a Killing field, that the inverse metrics are uniformly bounded,
or that $\rho_\varepsilon$ is positive; the latter properties are
consequences proved separately where they are used. The family is an explicit
input-family hypothesis: neither its existence for prescribed Newtonian
initial data nor its construction from other data is claimed. The physical
reading of the components, of $G_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$, of $\Phi$ and of
$\rho_\varepsilon$ belongs to the framework's postulates and unit
conventions, which are separate items.

items.title: Stationarity, timelikeness and uniform inverse-metric bounds for stationary weak-field data
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$ and compact $K\subseteq U$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]], [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]]),
and let $E(\varepsilon):=g(\varepsilon)-\eta$ and
$H(\varepsilon):=\eta^{-1}E(\varepsilon)$ be the component matrices of the
perturbation and of its $\eta$-raise. Let
$m(A):=\max_{a,b}|A_{ab}|$ denote the maximum-entry norm of a $4\times4$
matrix. Then with
$\varepsilon_*:=\min\{\varepsilon_0,\,1,\,(128C)^{-1}\}$ the following
hold at every $p\in\Omega$ with $\pi(p)\in K$ and every
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$:

**(a) Smallness, timelikeness and stationarity.** At these spacetime points,

$$m\bigl(E(\varepsilon)\bigr)\le4C\varepsilon,\qquad m\bigl(H(\varepsilon)\bigr)\le16C\varepsilon\le\tfrac18,\qquad g(\varepsilon)_{00}\le-\tfrac12 ,$$

so the chart field $\partial_0$ is timelike over the spatial compact $K$;
moreover $\partial_0$ is
a Killing field of $g(\varepsilon)$ on $\Omega$
([[def-gr-killing-field]]).

**(b) Inverse-metric expansion and uniform bounds.** There is
$C_1=C_1(C,L)<\infty$ such that at these spacetime points, with
$R^{ab}(\varepsilon):=g^{ab}(\varepsilon)-\eta^{ab}+\eta^{ac}E_{cd}(\varepsilon)\eta^{db}$,

$$|R^{ab}(\varepsilon)|\le C_1\varepsilon^2,\qquad |g^{ab}(\varepsilon)-\eta^{ab}|\le C_1\varepsilon,\qquad |\partial^\alpha g^{ab}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_1}{L^{|\alpha|}}\quad(1\le|\alpha|\le2),$$

and

$$|\partial^\alpha R^{ab}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_1\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}}\qquad(0\le|\alpha|\le2),$$

where $g^{ab}(\varepsilon)$ are the components of the inverse metric
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]).

items.title: Uniform Christoffel-symbol bounds for stationary weak-field data
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$, compact $K\subseteq U$, and spatial
potential $\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]), let $c>0$, and let
$\varepsilon_*$ and $C_1$ be the threshold and constant of
[[lem-gr-weak-field-admissibility-and-inverse-bounds]]. Then there is
$C_2<\infty$, depending only on $C$, $L$ and the dimension, such that for
every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$ the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ of the metric-selected connection of $g(\varepsilon)$ in
the inertial chart satisfy the following bounds at every spacetime point
$p\in\Omega$ with $\pi(p)\in K$:

$$\Bigl|\Gamma^i{}_{00}-\frac{\partial_i\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L},\qquad |\Gamma^i{}_{0j}|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L},\qquad |\Gamma^i{}_{jk}|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon}{L},$$

$$|\Gamma^0{}_{00}|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{5/2}}{L},\qquad |\Gamma^0{}_{0j}|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon}{L},\qquad |\Gamma^0{}_{jk}|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L},$$

for all $i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$, with the maximum over the free spatial indices.

items.title: The weak-field Einstein hierarchy: linearized Einstein tensor, stress components and the Poisson equation
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$ and compact $K\subseteq U$, and suppose the
data form an Einstein family with coupling $\kappa>0$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]] clauses (a)-(c)). Write
$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi:U\to\mathbb R$,
$\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2:U\to\mathbb R$, and let $G^{(1)}$ be the
first-order Einstein coefficient of
[[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]. Let $c>0$ and
$G_N:=\kappa c^4/(8\pi)$. There are $\varepsilon_*'>0$, depending only on $\varepsilon_0$, $C$,
$L$ and the dimension, and $C_2<\infty$, depending only on $C$, $L$ and
the dimension, such that for every
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*'$ the following inequalities hold at every
spacetime point $p\in\Omega$ with $\pi(p)\in K$. Spatial derivatives and
$\Delta$ are taken on $U$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), and maxima
are over the free component indices.

**(a) Linearized approximation.** With
$A_{ab}(\varepsilon):=g_{ab}(\varepsilon)-\eta_{ab}$,

$$\bigl|G_{ab}(g(\varepsilon))-G^{(1)}_{ab}(A(\varepsilon))\bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2} .$$

**(b) Component hierarchy of the Einstein tensor.**

$$\Bigl|G_{00}(g(\varepsilon))-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{ij}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{0i}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

**(c) Stress hierarchy and independent dust source.** The Einstein equation
gives

$$\Bigl|\kappa T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{ij}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |\kappa T_{0i}(\varepsilon)|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2}.$$

For every Einstein family, the definition $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$ therefore gives
$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\rho_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{2L^2}.$$

For the additional conclusion below, let $\nabla^\varepsilon$ denote the
metric-selected connection of $g(\varepsilon)$ and assume the Einstein source is an
**independent admissible nonnegative dust input**: for each $\varepsilon$,
there are smooth fields $\mathcal E_\varepsilon:\Omega\to[0,\infty)$ and
$u_\varepsilon$ on $\Omega$, with $u_\varepsilon$ future-directed and
$g(\varepsilon)(u_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)=-1$, such that
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon (u_\varepsilon)_a(u_\varepsilon)_b$ and
$$\nabla^\varepsilon_a(\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_\varepsilon^a)=0,\qquad u_\varepsilon^a\nabla^\varepsilon_a u_\varepsilon^b=0 .$$
Where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon>0$, this is the dust model of
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; where it vanishes, the smooth field
$u_\varepsilon$ remains specified and satisfies the geodesic equation by
the explicit hypotheses above. The stress
conservation identity follows from these equations (and agrees on the
positive-density region with [[prop-gr-dust-and-perfect-fluid-conservation-equations]]).
No comoving condition is imposed: the spatial tilt may be nonzero.
Define the independent rest-mass density
$$\mu_\varepsilon:=\mathcal E_\varepsilon/c^2\quad[\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}],$$
where $\mathcal E_\varepsilon$ has the rest-energy-density unit
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and $\mu_\varepsilon$ is independent of the
coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon$.
It factors through $\pi$: normalization gives $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=-g^{ab}T_{ab}=-\kappa^{-1}g^{ab}G_{ab}$, whose components factor through the spatial projection by the Einstein-family hypothesis. Thus $\mu_\varepsilon$ also denotes its resulting smooth spatial function on $U$, including on disconnected fibers.
On $K$, assume the explicit weak-source and tilted slow-motion bounds
$$0\le\mathcal E_\varepsilon\le\frac{C\varepsilon c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad s_\varepsilon\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\,c,$$
where on the region over $K$ the time orientation is chosen so that
$\partial_0$ is future (and $g(u_\varepsilon,\partial_0)<0$), and
$n_\varepsilon:=\partial_0/\sqrt{-g_{00}}$ is the resulting future unit
coordinate observer, $\gamma_\varepsilon:=-g(u_\varepsilon,n_\varepsilon)$,
$h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon):=u_\varepsilon+g(n_\varepsilon,u_\varepsilon)n_\varepsilon$,
and $s_\varepsilon$ is the norm of
$c\,h_{n_\varepsilon}(u_\varepsilon)/\gamma_\varepsilon$ in the observer's
rest space ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]],
[[lem-gr-observer-relative-velocity-expansions]]). Choose
$$\varepsilon_*'\le\min\{\varepsilon_0,1,(128C)^{-1},(4C^2)^{-1}\},$$
also small enough for the two-jet estimate in the proof. This threshold
condition is dimensionless.
Then, for a constant $C_d$ depending only on $C$,

$$|T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\mu_\varepsilon c^2|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^4}{G_NL^2},\qquad |\rho_\varepsilon-\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^2}{G_NL^2},$$

and the distinct dust rest-mass density satisfies the Poisson estimate

$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{L^2} .$$

The energy- and mass-density conventions of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]
give the same tensor here:
$T_{ab}=\mathcal E_\varepsilon u_a u_b=c^2\mu_\varepsilon u_a u_b$,
with $\mathcal E_\varepsilon=c^2\mu_\varepsilon$.

**(d) Scaled dust source.** Let $X:=\mathbf x/L$ and
$U_L:=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$. Define
$\psi(X):=\varphi(LX)$ and
$R(X):=G_NL^2\mu_\varepsilon(LX)/(\varepsilon c^2)$ on $U_L$, with
$\Delta_X$ the Laplacian in $X$. Then

$$|\Delta_X\psi-4\pi R|\le C_2\varepsilon\qquad\text{on }K/L .$$

items.title: Coordinate-time acceleration of weak-field geodesics: the Newtonian leading term with uniform error
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$, compact $K\subseteq U$ and spatial
potential $\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]), let $c>0$, let
$\varepsilon_*$ and $C_2$ be the threshold and constant of
[[lem-gr-weak-field-christoffel-bounds]], let
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$, and let $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the
Christoffel symbols of $g(\varepsilon)$ in the inertial chart.

**(a) Reparametrization identity.** Let $\gamma:S\to\Omega$ be a geodesic of
$g(\varepsilon)$ in an affine parameter $s$ on an interval $S$
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]), suppose that
$t(s):=x^0(\gamma(s))/c$ is $C^2$ with $dt/ds\ne0$ on $S$ and has image an
interval $I$, and write $x(t)$ for the spatial coordinates of $\gamma$ and
$z(t):=(ct,x(t))$ for its full chart-coordinate curve. Set
$u^a:=dz^a/dt=(c,\dot x)$; the geodesic equation holds in the chart
([[prop-coordinate-geodesic-equation]]). Then for every $t\in I$,

$$\frac{d^2x^i}{dt^2} =-\Gamma^i{}_{bc}u^bu^c+\frac{u^i}{c}\,\Gamma^0{}_{bc}u^bu^c .$$

**(b) Newtonian leading term.** Suppose in addition that
$\gamma(t)=(ct,x(t))\in\Omega$, $x(t)\in K$ and
$|\dot x(t)|\le C\sqrt\varepsilon\,c$ for every $t\in I$. Then there is
$C_3<\infty$, depending only on $C$, $L$ and the dimension, such that for
every $t\in I$ and $i=1,2,3$,

$$\Bigl|\frac{d^2x^i}{dt^2}+\partial_i\Phi\bigl(x(t)\bigr)\Bigr|\le\frac{C_3\,c^2\varepsilon^2}{L} .$$

items.title: Scaled trajectory limit: weak-field geodesics converge to the Newtonian system at rate O(epsilon)
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data
with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$, compact $K\subseteq U$, spatial potential
$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$ and $c>0$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]), let $\varepsilon_*$ and $C_2$ be
the threshold and constant of
[[lem-gr-weak-field-christoffel-bounds]], let $S_*>0$ and
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$, and put
$T_\varepsilon:=LS_*/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$,
$U_L:=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$, and
$\psi(X):=\varphi(LX)$ for $X\in U_L$.

Equip each $\mathbb R^3$ here with the Euclidean inner product
$\langle X,Y\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^3X^iY^i$ and norm
$\|X\|_2=\sqrt{\langle X,X\rangle}$
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). In the standard coordinates,
$\nabla\psi=(\partial_{X^1}\psi,\partial_{X^2}\psi,\partial_{X^3}\psi)$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]); write
$D^2\psi:=D(\nabla\psi)$ for its derivative and
$\|D^2\psi(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|D^2\psi(X)v\|_2$.

Suppose:

- **(H1)** there is an affinely parametrized geodesic of $g(\varepsilon)$ admitting
  a $C^2$ reparametrization $\gamma_\varepsilon$ by $t=x^0/c$ on
  $[0,T_\varepsilon]$, with $dt/ds\ne0$ in its affine parameter $s$,
  whose length-coordinate components are
  $\gamma_\varepsilon(t)=(ct,x_\varepsilon(t))\in\Omega$, with spatial
  trajectory $x_\varepsilon(t)\in K$ and
  $|\dot x_\varepsilon(t)|\le C\sqrt\varepsilon c$ for every such $t$;
- **(H2)** setting $t(S):=LS/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$,
  $X_\varepsilon(S):=x_\varepsilon(t(S))/L$ and
  $W_\varepsilon(S):=\dot x_\varepsilon(t(S))/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$ for
  $S\in[0,S_*]$, and letting $K'\subseteq U_L$ be a compact convex set
  containing every $X_\varepsilon(S)$, there is a $C^1$ map
  $(X_*,W_*):[0,S_*]\to\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3$ with
  $X_*([0,S_*])\subseteq K'$ and

$$X_*'(S)=W_*(S),\qquad W_*'(S)=-\nabla\psi\bigl(X_*(S)\bigr)\qquad(0\le S\le S_*);$$

- **(H3)** $\|D^2\psi(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le K_2$ for every $X\in K'$, where $K_2\ge0$.

Then for every $S\in[0,S_*]$, with
$D(S):=\|X_\varepsilon(S)-X_*(S)\|_2+\|W_\varepsilon(S)-W_*(S)\|_2$,

$$D(S)\le\bigl(D(0)+C_3\varepsilon S_*\bigr)\,e^{(1+K_2)S_*},$$

where $C_3$ depends only on $C$, $L$ and the dimension. Consequently the
following hold.

**(i) Convergence.** If $D(0)\to0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ along the
family, then $\sup_{0\le S\le S_*}D(S)\to0$.

**(ii) Rate for identical data.** If $D(0)=0$, then
$\sup_{0\le S\le S_*}D(S)\le C_3\varepsilon S_*e^{(1+K_2)S_*}=O(\varepsilon)$.

**(iii) Long coordinate times.** The coordinate-time horizon is
$T_\varepsilon=LS_*/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$, so the fixed scaled interval
$[0,S_*]$ corresponds to coordinate times growing like
$\varepsilon^{-1/2}$; the limit statement is therefore not a large-$t$
statement at fixed $\varepsilon$.

items.title: Low-velocity expansions of observer energy and momentum with uniform error bounds
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, $p\in M$,
$n$ an observer at $p$ and $P\in T_pM$ a future timelike vector with rest
mass $m:=m(P)>0$ ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]],
[[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $U:=P/m$, $u:=U/c$,
$\gamma:=-g_p(n,u)$ and, as in clause 3 of
[[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-identities]],

$$w:=\frac{c\,h_n(u)}{\gamma}\in n^\perp,\qquad s:=\sqrt{g_p(w,w)} .$$

For $z\in n^\perp$ write $|z|_n:=\sqrt{g_p(z,z)}$, the norm from the positive-definite restriction of $g_p$ to $n^\perp$. Thus $s=|w|_n$, and $|q_n(P)|$ in the displays below means $|q_n(P)|_n$; $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ by the observer decomposition.

Then $s<c$, $\gamma=(1-s^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$,

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2},\qquad |q_n(P)|=ms\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2},$$

and for every $0\le v_0<c$, with $z_0:=v_0^2/c^2<1$ and all $s\le v_0$,

$$\Bigl|E_n(P)-mc^2-\tfrac12ms^2\Bigr|\le\tfrac38\,(1-z_0)^{-5/2}\,\frac{ms^4}{c^2},\qquad \Bigl||q_n(P)|-ms\Bigr|\le\tfrac12\,(1-z_0)^{-3/2}\,\frac{ms^3}{c^2} .$$

items.title: Vanishing curvature on a normal neighborhood is a local isometry to Minkowski space
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and curvature $R$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let $p\in M$, let
$\mathcal E_p\subseteq T_pM$ be the exponential domain of
[[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]], let $W\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
be a star-shaped open neighborhood of $0$ on which $\exp_p$ is a
diffeomorphism onto the open set $U:=\exp_p(W)$, and suppose

$$R\equiv0\quad\text{on }U .$$

Let $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be a $g_p$-orthonormal basis of $T_pM$ and
$\psi:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ its coordinate isomorphism, and write
$\eta_{ab}:=g_p(e_a,e_b)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{ab}$
([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]]).

**(a) The differential of the exponential map is an isometry.** For every
$v\in W$ the differential
$d(\exp_p)_v:\bigl(T_pM,g_p\bigr)\to\bigl(T_{\exp_p(v)}M,g_{\exp_p(v)}\bigr)$
is a linear isometry ([[def-differential-of-a-smooth-map]]).

**(b) Local isometry.** The map $\exp_p:(W,g_p)\to(U,g)$ is an isometry of
the open subset $W$ of the flat vector space $(T_pM,g_p)$ onto $(U,g)$;
equivalently $\exp_p^*g=g_p$ on $W$.

**(c) Constant metric components.** In the exponential chart
$u:=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}:U\to\mathbb R^4$, the components of $g$ are the
constants $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$; hence the identity map of $u(U)$ with the
standard Minkowski form is an isometry of $U$ onto an open subset of
Minkowski space.

**(d) Open flat sets.** If $R\equiv0$ on an open set $O\subseteq M$ and
$p\in O$, then there is a star-shaped open $W_0\subseteq\mathcal E_p$ with
$\exp_p(W_0)\subseteq O$ for which (a)-(c) hold; in particular every point of
$O$ has a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of Minkowski space.

**(e) Converse direction.** Conversely, if an open set $V\subseteq M$ admits
a smooth chart in which $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$ are constant, then $R\equiv0$ on
$V$.

items.title: The Newtonian comparison model and the weak-field correspondence identification
items.statement:
This item defines the auxiliary framework used to formulate the Newtonian
bridge, and the dictionary by which the relativistic weak-field data are read
against it. It asserts no approximation; the approximation statement is a
separate theorem of this page.

**(a) Newtonian comparison model.** A **Newtonian comparison model** is a
tuple $(O,\Phi_N,\rho_N,G_{\mathrm{cmp}})$ consisting of

- a nonempty open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the **spatial region**, whose
  points are read as positions in metres;
- a $C^\infty$ function $\Phi_N:O\to\mathbb R$, the **Newtonian potential**,
  whose values are read in $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$;
- a $C^\infty$ function $\rho_N:O\to\mathbb R$, the **Newtonian mass
  density**, whose values are read in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; and
- a real constant $G_{\mathrm{cmp}}>0$ with the dimension
  $\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$,

such that the **Newtonian field equation**

$$\Delta\Phi_N=4\pi G_{\mathrm{cmp}}\rho_N\qquad\text{on }O$$

holds, where $\Delta$ is the Laplacian on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). A **comparison motion** of the model is
a $C^2$ curve $q:J\to O$ on an interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ whose points
are read as times in seconds, satisfying the **Newtonian equation of motion**

$$q''(t)=-\nabla\Phi_N\bigl(q(t)\bigr)\qquad(t\in J),$$

where in the standard coordinates of $\mathbb R^3$
$\nabla\Phi_N(q):=(\partial_1\Phi_N(q),\partial_2\Phi_N(q),\partial_3\Phi_N(q))$
([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]) and the total derivative is the
covector represented by this vector through the Euclidean inner product:
$D\Phi_N(q)[v]=\langle\nabla\Phi_N(q),v\rangle$
([[def-total-derivative-in-euclidean-space]],
[[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],
[[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).
The model is an auxiliary classical model: its equations are adopted as part
of the definition of the comparison framework and are not derived here from
the relativistic framework or from anything else.

**(b) The correspondence identification.** Let
$(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ be stationary weak-field data over
the spacetime region $\Omega$, with spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$, parameters
$c>0$ and $G_N>0$, an Einstein family, spatial potential
$\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$, and coordinate density
$\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}(\varepsilon)/c^2$ on $U$
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]],
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]],
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]). A **comparison reading** consists of a
Newtonian comparison model $(O,\Phi_N,\rho_N,G_{\mathrm{cmp}})$ and the
following adopted dictionary:

1. the Newtonian spatial region is $O=U$, the spatial projection of $\Omega$,
   and chart spatial coordinates in metres are read as Newtonian positions;
2. chart time $t=x^0/c$ in seconds is read as the Newtonian time parameter;
3. the spatial potential $\Phi:U\to\mathbb R$ is identified exactly with
   $\Phi_N$, both with units $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$;
4. the constants $G_N$ and $G_{\mathrm{cmp}}$ are identified exactly.

The Newtonian source density $\rho_N$ continues to satisfy its exact model
equation in clause (a). It is not identified here with either
$\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$ or a dust rest-mass density; no density error
estimate is part of this definition.

**(c) Status.** The dictionary of (b) is an **adopted correspondence
assumption**: it fixes which regions, coordinates, potentials and couplings
of the two frameworks are to be compared, in which units, and is part of the
formulation of any bridge statement built on it. The Newtonian source density
$\rho_N$, the relativistic coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon$ and a dust
rest-mass density are distinct quantities. Any error-qualified matching
between them is a separate theorem under its own hypotheses. This definition
neither asserts exact density equality nor agreement of the models, and it
does not assert that either framework describes nature.

**(d) Scope and exclusions.** The comparison model is smooth and
source-continuous: point masses and delta densities are excluded, no boundary
conditions at spatial infinity are imposed, and no statement is made about
the numerical value, sign convention or uncertainty of $G_N$, $G_{\mathrm{cmp}}$
or $c$; those belong to the framework's conventions and to empirical work
elsewhere. The comparison model has no relativistic content: it carries no
metric, no causal structure and no stress-energy tensor, and its
identification with the weak-field data is confined to the items listed in
(b).

items.title: The Minkowski vacuum model with Lambda = 0: field law, free-fall kinematics and clock readings
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]],
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, with the field law in its direct-equation presentation. Let
$(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$, let
$\Lambda:=0$ and let the model's stress-energy tensor be the vacuum
prescription

$$T:=0\qquad\text{on }M .$$

Then all statements below are conditional deductions inside the model so
specified; they assert nothing about nature.

**(a) The flat vacuum model.** $(M,g,N)$ satisfies the spacetime postulate,
$T=0$ is a smooth symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the matter domain
$M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], the prescription
$T=0$ is admissible, and the adopted field law
$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds identically on $M$; in the
notation of [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]] clause (d)
this is its flat vacuum solution, here read as a model of the framework.

**(b) Free fall and clocks.** Let $p\in M$ and let $U_0\in T_pM$ be future
timelike with $g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$. In the inertial chart write
$x(p)=x_0$ and $U_0=c\,v$ with $\eta(v,v)=-1$ and $v^0>0$. Then the physical worldline of an
ideal freely falling massive test body released at $p$ with four-velocity
$U_0$, with proper-time origin at release, is a restriction to its actual
proper-time interval $I\ni0$ of the unique maximal mathematical straight
geodesic on $\mathbb R$

$$x\bigl(\gamma(\tau)\bigr)=x_0+v\,c\,\tau$$

($\tau$ proper time, so $x^0$ is measured in metres along $c\tau$); its
coordinate velocity is the constant $w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ with
$|w|<c$; and an ideal clock carried along it reads, between two coordinate
times $t_0<t_1$ within that physical worldline's domain,

$$\Delta\tau=\sqrt{1-\frac{|w|^2}{c^2}}\;(t_1-t_0),\qquad t=x^0/c .$$

The maximal geodesic continuation is determined by $(p,U_0)$ alone; the
free-fall postulate does not require the body's physical domain to be maximal.

**(c) No tidal response.** Every free-fall congruence of this model has
vanishing relative acceleration: $D_\tau^2J=0$, since the curvature vanishes
identically.

**(d) Scope.** The model is an idealized vacuum model of the framework, not a
claim about the actual universe: no observation, apparatus, calibration or
uncertainty is used, and no comparison with data is made. The flat model
solves the field law with the chosen parameters $(\Lambda,T)=(0,0)$; other
solutions of the same field law exist and are not excluded, and flat
solutions with different global topology exist as well (see the scope remark
of this page). The physical interpretation of coordinates, clocks and bodies
remains the adopted one of the cited postulates.

items.title: The controlled weak-field slow-motion correspondence with the Newtonian comparison model
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]],
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] in the direct-equation presentation and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. Let stationary weak-field data
$(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ over spacetime region $\Omega$ have
spatial base $U=\pi(\Omega)$, form an Einstein family with
$\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$, and satisfy the independent admissible nonnegative
slow-dust hypotheses in clause (c) of
[[thm-gr-weak-field-einstein-stress-hierarchy]]. Write $\mu_\varepsilon$ for
that dust rest-mass density. Let a comparison reading with a Newtonian
comparison model $(U,\Phi_N,\rho_N,G_{\mathrm{cmp}})$ be adopted under
[[def-gr-newtonian-comparison-model-and-identification]], so that
$\Phi_N=\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$ and $G_{\mathrm{cmp}}=G_N$; the
Newtonian model satisfies its exact Poisson equation
$\Delta\Phi_N=4\pi G_{\mathrm{cmp}}\rho_N$ by definition.

Let $\varepsilon_*'$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ be the thresholds and constants of
[[thm-gr-weak-field-einstein-stress-hierarchy]],
[[lem-gr-weak-field-christoffel-bounds]] and
[[lem-gr-weak-field-geodesic-acceleration]]. Let $S_*>0$,
$0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*'$, and put
$T_\varepsilon=LS_*/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$ and
$U_L=\{X\in\mathbb R^3:LX\in U\}$,
$\psi(X)=\varphi(LX)$ on $U_L$. Assume there are an ideal freely falling
massive test body worldline $\gamma_\varepsilon$ and its spatial coordinate
curve $x_\varepsilon:[0,T_\varepsilon]\to U$ such that
$\gamma_\varepsilon(t)=(ct,x_\varepsilon(t))\in\Omega$,
$x_\varepsilon(t)\in K$, and
$|\dot x_\varepsilon(t)|\le C\sqrt\varepsilon c$.
Suppose also that hypotheses (H2)-(H3) of
[[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]] hold on a compact convex
$K'\subseteq U_L$ containing both scaled trajectory ranges, with
$K_2=\sup_{X\in K'}\|D^2\psi(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\infty$,
using the Euclidean vector norm and induced Hessian operator norm fixed in
[[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]].

Then the following are conditional consequences of the adopted postulates,
the independent coupled Einstein-dust input, the comparison dictionary and
the stated mathematical hypotheses. No family or dust solution is asserted
to exist for prescribed Newtonian data.

**(a) Field and source correspondence.** At every $\mathbf x\in K$,

$$\Bigl|\kappa T_{00}(\varepsilon)-\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2}\Bigr|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{ij}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2}{L^2},\qquad |G_{0i}(g(\varepsilon))|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^2},$$

and the distinct source densities satisfy

$$|\Delta\Phi-4\pi G_N\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{L^2},\qquad |\rho_N-\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_2\varepsilon^2c^2}{4\pi G_NL^2},\qquad |\rho_\varepsilon-\mu_\varepsilon|\le\frac{C_d\varepsilon^2c^2}{G_NL^2},$$

where $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$ is the relativistic coordinate density and $\mu_\varepsilon$ is the independently specified dust rest-mass density. The comparison model's Poisson equation remains exact; the approximation is the density matching.

**(b) Free-fall kinematics.** The assigned worldline $\gamma_\varepsilon$ is a future timelike geodesic of $g(\varepsilon)$ with $g(U_\varepsilon,U_\varepsilon)=-c^2$, proper time an affine parameter, and initial data determining the worldline. On the stated coordinate-time interval,

$$\Bigl|\ddot x^i_\varepsilon(t)+\partial_i\Phi(x_\varepsilon(t))\Bigr|\le\frac{C_3c^2\varepsilon^2}{L}\qquad(t\in[0,T_\varepsilon]).$$

**(c) Trajectory correspondence.** With
$X_\varepsilon(S)=x_\varepsilon(LS/(\sqrt\varepsilon c))/L$,
$W_\varepsilon(S)=\dot x_\varepsilon(LS/(\sqrt\varepsilon c))/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$,
and $(X_*,W_*)$ the comparison motion of (H2), let
$D(S)=\|X_\varepsilon(S)-X_*(S)\|_2+\|W_\varepsilon(S)-W_*(S)\|_2$
using the same Euclidean norm convention.
Then

$$D(S)\le\bigl(D(0)+C_3\varepsilon S_*\bigr)e^{(1+K_2)S_*}\qquad(0\le S\le S_*).$$

Thus convergent scaled initial data give uniform convergence on the fixed
scaled interval, and identical scaled data give a uniform $O(\varepsilon)$
error. The corresponding coordinate times
$t=LS/(\sqrt\varepsilon c)$ grow like $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$.

**(d) Status and qualifications.** This is a conditional comparison of an
Einstein family containing an independently specified conserved tilted dust
source with an auxiliary Newtonian model. It does not derive the Newtonian
model, does not establish that either model describes nature, and uses no
observations, apparatus, calibration or measured constant. The input family
and dust fields are hypotheses; the theorem proves neither their existence
nor uniqueness for prescribed Newtonian data. Any empirical value of $G_N$
and comparison with data would require separate uncertainty-qualified
empirical premises.

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), sections 5.1-5.1.2: the weak-field slow-motion correspondence, the Poisson equation and the particle acceleration, printed pp. 205-210 (PDF pp. 212-217)

items.physical_scope: Conditional model-to-model correspondence inside the classical gravitational framework: given an Einstein family of spatially factored stationary weak-field data with an independent admissible nonnegative tilted dust source satisfying explicit weak-source and slow-tilt bounds, and a comparison reading against a Newtonian comparison model, the field hierarchy gives an error-qualified match between the Newtonian model's exact Poisson source and the dust rest-mass density; ideal test-body geodesics also converge to the comparison motions with a uniform O(epsilon) error on a fixed scaled time interval. Excludes: existence of the input family from prescribed Newtonian data, strong fields, fast motion, long-time or global limits, observational comparisons, measured values of constants, non-smooth or distributional sources, and any claim that the model or the correspondence describes nature. All conclusions are conditional on the adopted postulates and the stated hypotheses.

items.title: Local flatness at a point, vanishing curvature and global Minkowski geometry are three different statements
items.statement:
This note separates three statements that are frequently conflated, and
records their exact status in this library; it proves nothing by itself.

- **First-order flatness at a point is automatic.** Every smooth Lorentzian
  four-manifold has point-normal and exponential charts in which
  $g_{ab}(p)=\eta_{ab}$, $\partial_ag_{bc}(p)=0$ and
  $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}(p)=0$; the construction is first order and makes no claim
  about second derivatives of the metric
  ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]] clauses (a)-(b)).
  Consequently the existence of locally inertial coordinates at an event is
  a property of every smooth metric, not an indication of vanishing
  curvature, and by itself it is not the statement that any neighborhood is
  Minkowski space.

- **The curvature is the second-order obstruction.** The point-normal formula
  of [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (c)
  expresses the curvature at the point through the second derivatives of the
  metric in any point-normal chart, and the curvature is a tensor field, so
  its vanishing is chart-independent
  ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the curvature
  vanishes on a normal neighborhood, the exponential chart is flat to all
  orders: the exponential map is an isometry onto an open subset of
  Minkowski space
  ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] clauses (a)-(d)).
  This is the exact sense in which a flat metric is *locally* Minkowski.

- **Global Minkowski geometry is strictly stronger.** Vanishing curvature on
  a manifold does not determine its topology, its holonomy or its causal
  structure. The companion examples page exhibits a flat
  Lorentzian quotient of Minkowski space by a translation whose time
  coordinate is periodic: the metric is flat, the Einstein tensor vanishes,
  yet the manifold is not diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^4$, admits closed
  timelike curves, and carries no global inertial chart; the theorem above is
  local precisely because it uses a normal neighborhood, not the whole
  manifold. Statements such as "the flat model is the spacetime" therefore
  require additional global hypotheses (simple connectedness, completeness,
  injectivity of the exponential map, a global chart) that are not part of
  the local computations of this page.

- **The flat model and its Killing structure.** In the model of
  [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] the coordinate fields
  $\partial_0,\dots,\partial_3$ are global Killing fields and the geodesics
  are complete straight lines
  ([[lem-gr-flat-model-connection-curvature-and-geodesics]] clauses (c)-(d)).
  A manifold merely locally isometric to this model need not inherit any of
  these global structures: local isometries do not glue to global ones
  without monodromy and completeness hypotheses. This is why the physical
  and mathematical statements of this page are phrased neighborhood by
  neighborhood.

- **Scope.** No classification of flat Lorentzian four-manifolds and no
  global rigidity statement is made or used on this page. The note only
  fixes which of the three statements above each item of the page proves,
  and warns that the words "locally flat", "curvature-free" and "Minkowski"
  are not interchangeable.

Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (1997), Ch. 2: Riemann normal coordinates, g(p)=eta and vanishing first derivatives; the warning that curvature obstructs making second derivatives vanish and that flat curvature does not fix global topology, printed pp. 50-51 (PDF pp. 57-58) and pp. 77-78 (PDF pp. 84-85)

D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), section 3.3.2: normal coordinates make the metric first-order flat, second derivatives cannot generally vanish, and curvature is the local obstruction; global topology is independent, printed pp. 119-121 (PDF pp. 126-128)

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the flat and Newtonian bridge page
items.statement:
This note fixes what the physics items of this page do and do not claim; it
proves nothing by itself.

- **The flat model is a model.** [[pthm-gr-minkowski-vacuum-model]] shows
  that the flat geometry with $\Lambda=0$ and $T=0$ satisfies the adopted
  field law and what its ideal free-fall and clock readings are. It is one
  solution among many: non-flat solutions, flat solutions with other global
  topology and the semiclassical or observational questions attached to
  "empty space" are outside this page. Statements about the flat model are
  conditional on the adopted postulates of
  [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], and are not claims about nature.

- **The bridge is a controlled comparison of models.** The weak-field results
  of this page — the Einstein and stress hierarchy
  ([[thm-gr-weak-field-einstein-stress-hierarchy]]), the geodesic
  acceleration estimate ([[lem-gr-weak-field-geodesic-acceleration]]) and
  the scaled trajectory convergence
  ([[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]]) — are estimates inside an
  explicitly hypothesized family of spatially factored stationary metrics
  ([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]). Their hypotheses are essential: an
  existing Einstein family with the stated derivative bounds, the
  slow-motion condition $|\dot x|\le C\sqrt\varepsilon c$, a common compact
  spatial region, a comparison motion that exists on the whole finite scaled
  interval and a bounded second derivative of the potential. The Poisson
  source match to dust rest-mass density additionally assumes the stated
  nonnegative dust model, its conservation equations, weak-source bound and
  slow tilt. The page does not
  construct the input family from Newtonian initial data, does not prove
  existence of a global Newtonian limit in any gauge, and does not treat
  strong fields, fast motion, long times or non-smooth sources.

- **The correspondence dictionary is adopted, not derived.**
  [[def-gr-newtonian-comparison-model-and-identification]] fixes the spatial
  region, time, potential and coupling dictionary. Its Newtonian source
  $\rho_N$ obeys its own exact Poisson equation and is not defined to equal
  either the relativistic coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon=T_{00}/c^2$
  or the independent dust rest-mass density $\mu_\varepsilon$. The conditional
  theorem [[pthm-gr-uniform-weak-slow-correspondence]] proves that $\rho_N$
  and $\rho_\varepsilon$ each match $\mu_\varepsilon$ within explicit errors
  under the dust hypotheses. No derivation of either framework from the
  other is claimed, and the identification of the geometric and potential
  variables is not an identity of theories.

- **The displayed spatial form is chart-dependent.** The perturbation form
  $g_{00}=-(1+2\Phi/c^2)+r_{00}$, $g_{ij}=(1-2\Phi/c^2)\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}$ is a statement
  in the chart of the ansatz. Under a change of chart the components
  transform by the covariant transformation law
  ([[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]]), so comparisons of
  spatial coefficients computed in different charts — for instance the
  areal-radius forms used in the spherical model — require the explicit
  coordinate conversion and are not identities; that conversion is deferred
  to the spherical-model page. Similarly, the gauge transformation of the
  flat linearization is a change of perturbation inside a fixed chart and is
  not a change of chart.

- **Kinematics versus dynamics.** The low-velocity expansions
  [[lem-gr-observer-relative-velocity-expansions]] and the observer energy
  and momentum definitions
  ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]) are kinematic: they
  expand the model's energy and momentum readings. The page does not prove
  conservation of any total energy. The Newtonian source density,
  coordinate density $\rho_\varepsilon$ and rest-mass density
  $\mu_\varepsilon$ are distinct objects; the weak-slow theorem gives only
  the stated conditional error bounds between them.

- **No measured input and no observations.** Nothing on the page uses a
  measured value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$; the unit conventions
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]] fix dimensions and
  normalizations only. A comparison with reported Newtonian, solar-system,
  clock, redshift or gravitational-wave data would require, in addition: the
  measured value of $G_N$ with its uncertainty and calibration, the
  apparatus and sampling model, an identified observable computed from the
  model, and a statistical account distinguishing prediction, observation
  and inference. Agreement of such a comparison would be evidence about the
  combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the postulates.
  None of that material is supplied on this page; the empirical interface is
  developed, if at all, on the track's later experimental pages with
  source-backed primary reports.

items.physical_scope: Scope and status note for the flat and Newtonian bridge material: the status of the flat Minkowski model, the conditional nature of the weak-field correspondence, its hypotheses and error terms, the chart dependence of the displayed spatial form, and the empirical qualifications required before any comparison with reported data. The note asserts no law, no solution, no measurement and no empirical fact.

items.title: First-order curvature of the diagonal perturbation h_00 = -2 phi, h_ij = -2 phi delta_ij for the explicit potential phi = |x|^2/2
items.statement:
Work on the flat model of [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with
its inertial chart $x$ and take for $\Omega$ the open unit ball of
$\mathbb R^4$ (identified with its image under $x$). Take the flat linearized
family of [[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]] with normalized remainder
$q\equiv0$ and first-order perturbation

$$h_{00}=-2\varphi,\qquad h_{ij}=-2\varphi\,\delta_{ij},\qquad h_{0i}=0,\qquad \varphi(x):=\tfrac12\bigl((x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2\bigr),$$

so that $g(\lambda)_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+\lambda\,h_{ab}$. Then
$(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ with $\varepsilon_1:=1/8$ and $q\equiv0$ is a flat
linearized family over $\Omega$, and with all indices raised and lowered by
$\eta$:

1. $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{00}=x^i$,
   $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{0j}=\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{j0}=0$ and
   $\Gamma^{(1)i}{}_{jk}=-\delta^i_k\,x_j-\delta^i_j\,x_k+\delta_{jk}\,x^i$,
   while $\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{00}=\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{ij}=0$ and
   $\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{0i}=\Gamma^{(1)0}{}_{i0}=x_i$; here
   $x_j:=\delta_{jm}x^m$, and $i,j,k$ range over $1,2,3$.
2. $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{00}=3$,
   $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{0i}=0$,
   $\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ij}=3\delta_{ij}$ and $S^{(1)}=6$.
3. The trace-reversed perturbation is
   $\bar h_{00}=-4\varphi$, $\bar h_{0i}=0$, $\bar h_{ij}=0$, and the closed
   formula of [[thm-gr-flat-linearized-curvature-and-gauge]] clause (c)
   gives $G^{(1)}_{00}=2\Delta\varphi=6$ and
   $G^{(1)}_{0i}=G^{(1)}_{ij}=0$; these values satisfy
   $G^{(1)}_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}^{(1)}_{ab}-\tfrac12\eta_{ab}S^{(1)}$ with
   the tensors of clause 2, as the first-order expansion of
   $G=\operatorname{Ric}-\tfrac12Sg$
   ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]) requires.

items.title: Straight timelike geodesics of the flat model: constant coordinate velocity, four-velocity and the clock-reading identity
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$, and
let $c>0$. Take the initial event $p$ with $x(p)=0$ and the tangent vector

$$U_0:=c\,v,\qquad v:=\Bigl(\frac{2}{\sqrt3},\frac{1}{\sqrt3},0,0\Bigr),\qquad \eta(v,v)=-1,\quad v^0>0,$$

so that $g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ and $U_0$ is future timelike. Then:

1. The maximal geodesic of the metric-selected connection with
   $x(\gamma(0))=0$ and velocity $v$ at $0$ is
   $x(\gamma(s))=s\,v$ on $\mathbb R$; it is a future timelike worldline, and
   $\tau(s)=s/c$ is its proper time up to an additive constant, with
   $d\gamma/d\tau=c\,v=U_0$ and $g(d\gamma/d\tau,d\gamma/d\tau)=-c^2$.
2. Its coordinate velocity in the parametrization $t=x^0/c$ is the constant
   $w=(c/2,0,0)$ and $|w|=c/2<c$.
3. Between coordinate times $t_0<t_1$ the proper time elapsed on the
   worldline is
   $\Delta\tau=\sqrt{1-|w|^2/c^2}\,(t_1-t_0)=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}(t_1-t_0)$,
   and this agrees with the direct parametrization $t=v^0\tau$.

items.title: An exact observer-relative energy and momentum computation at relative speed c/2, with the expansion bounds of the low-velocity lemma checked by exact rational comparison
items.statement:
Work on the flat model of [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with
inertial chart $x$ and let $c>0$ and $m>0$. At $p$ with $x(p)=0$ take the
observer $n:=\partial_0|_p$ and the tangent vector

$$P:=mc\,u,\qquad u:=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}\,\partial_0|_p+\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\,\partial_1|_p ,$$

so that $g_p(u,u)=-1$ and $P$ is future timelike with rest mass $m$
([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]). Then the observer data of
the low-velocity lemma are

$$h_n(u)=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\,\partial_1|_p,\qquad \gamma=\frac{2}{\sqrt3},\qquad w=\frac c2\,\partial_1|_p,\qquad s=\frac c2,$$

and the exact energy and momentum are

$$E_n(P)=\frac{2mc^2}{\sqrt3},\qquad q_n(P)=\frac{mc}{\sqrt3}\,\partial_1|_p,\qquad |q_n(P)|=\frac{mc}{\sqrt3}.$$

With $v_0:=c/2$, $z_0=1/4$ this realizes $s=v_0<c$ and the exact identities

$$E_n(P)=mc^2\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2},\qquad |q_n(P)|=ms\Bigl(1-\frac{s^2}{c^2}\Bigr)^{-1/2}$$

of [[lem-gr-observer-relative-velocity-expansions]], and the two uniform error
bounds of that lemma read

$$\Bigl|E_n(P)-mc^2-\tfrac12ms^2\Bigr|=\frac{mc^2(16-9\sqrt3)}{8\sqrt3}\le\frac{mc^2}{12\sqrt3},\qquad \Bigl||q_n(P)|-ms\Bigr|=\frac{mc(2-\sqrt3)}{2\sqrt3}\le\frac{mc}{6\sqrt3},$$

which are strict, finite checks of the bounds at the single relative speed
$s=c/2$.

items.title: Explicit stationary weak-field data with a dimensionless quadratic potential: exact Poisson source and the first-order Einstein coefficient
items.statement:
Work on the flat model of [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with
inertial chart $x$, let $L>0$ be a length, take spacetime region
$\Omega=\mathbb R\times B_L(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with spatial base
$U=B_L(0)\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, and let $K=\overline B_{L/2}(0)\subset U$.
Set $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, $C:=1$,
$\varepsilon_0:=1/2$, choose the stationary-data remainder interval parameter
$\varepsilon_1^{\mathrm{data}}:=1$, set $r\equiv0$ on that interval, and

$$\varphi(\mathbf x):=\frac{(x^1)^2+(x^2)^2+(x^3)^2}{2L^2}.$$

Then:

1. $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is stationary weak-field data
   in the sense of [[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]] clause (a), with
   $g_{ab}(\varepsilon)=\eta_{ab}+\varepsilon h_{ab}$,
   $h_{00}=-2\varphi$, $h_{ij}=-2\varphi\delta_{ij}$, $h_{0i}=0$; the
   family $(\delta_1,h,q)$ with $\delta_1:=1/2$ and $q\equiv0$ is
   a flat linearized family and $g(\varepsilon)-\eta=\varepsilon h$.
2. Defining $T_{ab}(\varepsilon):=G_{ab}(g(\varepsilon))/\kappa$ and
   $\rho_\varepsilon:=T_{00}(\varepsilon)/c^2$
   ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]) makes the data an
   **Einstein family with coupling $\kappa$**
   ([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]] clause (c)). This smooth symmetric
   source is defined by the metric; no dust model or independent rest-mass
   density is asserted.
3. For $\Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi$,
   $\Delta\Phi=3\varepsilon c^2/L^2$ exactly. The constant Newtonian source

   $$\bar\rho:=\frac{3\varepsilon c^2}{4\pi G_NL^2}$$

   satisfies $\Delta\Phi=4\pi G_N\bar\rho$ exactly on $U$. The distinct
   coordinate density read from the Einstein-family tensor satisfies
   $|\rho_\varepsilon-\bar\rho|\le C_2\varepsilon^2c^2/(8\pi G_NL^2)$ on
   $K$ for $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*'$, by the general $00$-component
   hierarchy; this does not use the hierarchy theorem's independent-dust
   conclusion.
4. The first-order Einstein coefficient of $A(\varepsilon):=\varepsilon h$
   is

   $$G^{(1)}_{00}(A(\varepsilon))=\frac{6\varepsilon}{L^2}=\frac{2\Delta\Phi}{c^2},\qquad G^{(1)}_{0i}(A(\varepsilon))=G^{(1)}_{ij}(A(\varepsilon))=0,$$

   so the leading term of the hierarchy is exactly the first-order
   coefficient of the family.

items.title: The scaled Newtonian comparison system for the quadratic potential: explicit harmonic solutions, a compact convex range and the hypotheses of the scaled trajectory theorem
items.statement:
Work on the flat model with inertial chart $x$, let $L>0$ be a length,
$\Omega=\mathbb R\times B_{2L}(0)$ with spatial base $U=B_{2L}(0)$, and
$K=\overline B_{L/2}(0)\subset U$. Set $C:=1$, $\varepsilon_0:=1/16$,
$r\equiv0$ and

$$\varphi(\mathbf x):=\frac{|\mathbf x|^2}{2L^2},\qquad \Phi=\varepsilon c^2\varphi.$$

Every unmarked norm $|\cdot|$ of a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ below means
$\|\cdot\|_2$ from the Euclidean inner product
([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). The gradient is the coordinate vector of
partial derivatives ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]), and the Hessian
bound below uses the induced operator norm $\|D^2\psi\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ of
[[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]].

These are stationary weak-field data
([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]). The scaled spatial base is
$U_L=B_2(0)$ and the scaled potential is

$$\psi(X)=\varphi(LX)=\tfrac12|X|^2,\qquad \nabla\psi(X)=X,\qquad D^2\psi=I_3.$$

For any $S_*>0$ and initial vectors $X_0,W_0\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfying
$R_0:=|X_0|+|W_0|<2$, the Newtonian comparison system of
[[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]]

$$X_*'(S)=W_*(S),\qquad W_*'(S)=-\nabla\psi(X_*(S))=-X_*(S)$$

has the solution

$$X_*(S)=\cos S\,X_0+\sin S\,W_0,\qquad W_*(S)=-\sin S\,X_0+\cos S\,W_0.$$

Its spatial range is contained in $\overline B_{R_0}(0):=\{X:\|X\|_2\le R_0\}$,
with $\overline B_0(0)=\{0\}$. Set
$R':=\max\{1/2,R_0\}<2$ and $K':=\overline B_{R'}(0)$. This is a compact
convex subset of $U_L$ containing the comparison trajectory. For the
trajectory estimate take $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_*$ from
[[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]]. If (H1) holds,
then $X_\varepsilon(S)\in\overline B_{1/2}(0)\subseteq K'$ as well, so (H2)
and (H3) hold with $K_2=1$. With matched scaled initial data, the conclusion
(ii) of the scaled trajectory theorem gives
$\sup_{[0,S_*]}D(S)\le C_3\varepsilon S_*e^{2S_*}=O(\varepsilon)$.

items.title: A first-order vacuum family whose exact metric has nonzero Ricci tensor at order epsilon^2: a harmonic diagonal perturbation with phi = x^1
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ be a flat linearized family over an
open set $\Omega$ of the flat model
([[def-gr-flat-linearized-perturbation]]) whose first-order Einstein tensor
vanishes identically, $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ on $\Omega$. Then every metric
$g(\lambda)$ of the family with $0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$ is an exact vacuum
solution of the field equation, $G_{ab}(g(\lambda))=0$ on $\Omega$."

The counterexample is the flat linearized family over the open unit ball
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ with

$$h_{00}=-2\varphi,\qquad h_{ij}=-2\varphi\,\delta_{ij},\qquad h_{0i}=0,\qquad \varphi(x):=x^1,\qquad q\equiv0,\qquad \varepsilon_1:=\tfrac14 ,$$

so that $g(\lambda)_{ab}=\eta_{ab}+\lambda h_{ab}$. Then:

1. $(\varepsilon_1,h,q)$ is a flat linearized family over $\Omega$, and
   $\varphi$ is harmonic, $\Delta\varphi=0$;
2. $G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$ on $\Omega$, so the hypothesis of the refuted statement
   holds, and by linearity $G^{(1)}_{ab}(\lambda h)=\lambda G^{(1)}_{ab}(h)=0$;
3. nevertheless the exact Ricci tensor of $g(\lambda)$ does not vanish: in
   closed form, with $p:=1+2\lambda\varphi$ and $q:=1-2\lambda\varphi$,

   $$\operatorname{Ric}_{00}\bigl(g(\lambda)\bigr)=-\frac{2\lambda^2}{p\,q^2}\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

   which equals $-2\lambda^2\neq0$ at the origin $x=0$ for every
   $0<|\lambda|<\varepsilon_1$; hence $G_{ab}(g(\lambda))\neq0$ on $\Omega$ and
   the conclusion of the refuted statement fails.

items.title: A flat Lorentzian four-manifold that is not isometric to Minkowski space: the rolled-up flat model R^4 / Z by a timelike translation
items.statement:
Statement refuted: "Let $(M,g,N)$ be a connected time-oriented smooth Lorentzian
four-manifold whose metric-selected connection has vanishing curvature,
$R\equiv0$ on $M$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Then $(M,g)$ is isometric
to Minkowski space $(\mathbb R^4,\eta)$: there is a diffeomorphism
$F:M\to\mathbb R^4$ with $F^*\eta=g$."

The counterexample is the quotient of the flat model by the timelike
translation group. Let $(\hat M,\hat g,\hat N)$ be the flat model
([[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]]) with inertial chart $x$, fix
$L>0$, let $\Gamma:=\mathbb Z$ act on $\hat M$ by

$$n\cdot p:=x^{-1}\bigl(x^0(p)+nL,\,x^1(p),\,x^2(p),\,x^3(p)\bigr),$$

and let $(M,g,N)$ be the quotient time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
constructed below with orbit map $q:\hat M\to M$, descended metric
$q^*g=\hat g$ and field $N_{q(p)}=dq_p(\hat N_p)$. Then:

1. $(M,g,N)$ is a connected smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold;
2. $(M,g)$ is flat: $R\equiv0$ for the metric-selected connection of $g$;
3. $M$ contains a nonconstant closed future timelike curve
   $\sigma:[0,L]\to M$, $\sigma(s):=q\bigl(x^{-1}(s,0,0,0)\bigr)$, with
   $\sigma(L)=\sigma(0)$ and $g(\sigma',\sigma')=-1$;
4. nevertheless there is **no** diffeomorphism $F:M\to\mathbb R^4$ with
   $F^*\eta=g$: $M$ is not isometric to Minkowski space, and in particular it
   admits no global chart in which the metric components are the constants
   $\eta_{ab}$.
